Palmer —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by a couple of options so you can pick the path that maps to your procurement model:

1) Evidence delivery (audit logs, SOC artifact package): we generally treat this as an implementation deliverable. Option A = one‑time implementation fee with a partial credit applied as a contra‑charge over the first 6 months (we call this the "evidence credit" approach). Option B = amortize the implementation fee fully as a pre‑paid credit applied against the first 12 months of recurring charges. We can model both.

2) On‑prem ops fee (HSM management + on‑prem gateway): typically recurring monthly. If you select the evidence credit Option A, we can offset up to 50% of the first 3 months of the on‑prem ops fee (pilot concession) to help with the ramp.

3) SLA for evidence delivery: standard window is 15 business days for full SOC/package evidence. We can commit to 10 business days as a paid upgrade (one‑time fee) or as a contractual SLA if you take the 12‑month amortization path.

I'll loop in Ben for pricing specifics and Jonas for procurement/PO formatting.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Palmer — Vanessa —

Following Vanessa's note, attached is a short pricing illustration and two concrete contract language snippets (one for the 6‑month contra credit, one for 12‑month amortization). Highlights:

- Option A (6‑month contra credit): Implementation evidence package = $48,000 one‑time. We apply $8,000/month credit to invoice lines for months 1‑6. On‑prem ops fee remains $7,500/month; first 3 months can be offset up to 50% if you elect the pilot concession.
- Option B (12‑month amortize): Implementation evidence package = recognized as a prepaid credit of $48,000 applied at $4,000/month across months 1‑12. No upfront offset to on‑prem ops fee, but total present value is the same.
- 10‑day evidence SLA: one‑time fee of $6,000 (waived if you commit to 24 months and take Option B).

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the sketches. A few clarifying asks from procurement/legal:

- The team prefers Option B (12‑month amortization) because it maps cleanly to our budget line for security spend. Can you produce an invoice example showing the prepaid credit applied monthly and the remaining on‑prem ops fee net of the credit? That will speed legal sign‑off.
- Regarding the 10‑day SLA fee: CompliantHealth is prepared to sign 24 months but would ask you to waive the $6,000 SLA fee in exchange for a 6‑month early termination clause tied to regulatory changes. Is that something Redwood can accept?
- On evidence delivery format: please confirm that audit logs will be ingested via S3 PUT and that the SOC artifact bundle will be delivered as a secure download link (DocuSign acceptance required on receipt). We will need evidence hashes (SHA‑256) for chain of custody.

If you can send the invoice example and the amended DocuSign language, procurement will route to legal today. PO expected within 48 hours of sign‑off.
